record.context_brief: Ultrapowers versus group von Neumann algebras
record.original_question: Can an ultrapower N^U of a II_1 factor ever be isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra?

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Is NU ever isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor (a von Neumann algebra with trivial center, separable predual, and a faithful normal tracial state $\tau$, infinite-dimensional and finite). Fix a free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and form the tracial ultrapower
$$N^{\mathcal{U}} \;=\; \ell^\infty(\mathbb{N}, N) \,/\, \{(x_n)_n : \lim_{n \to \mathcal{U}} \tau(x_n^* x_n) = 0\},$$
which is again a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor (in general non-separable). Recall that for a discrete group $G$, the group von Neumann algebra $L(G)$ is the weak-operator closure of the left regular representation of $G$ on $\ell^2(G)$; when $G$ is i.c.c. (every nontrivial conjugacy class is infinite), $L(G)$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

Question: Does there exist a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$, a free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and a discrete group $G$ such that the ultrapower $N^{\mathcal{U}}$ is $*$-isomorphic to the group von Neumann algebra $L(G)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. It is listed as one of 50 open problems concerning ultrapower II_1 factors, and related questions (such as whether the ultrapower of the hyperfinite II_1 factor is isomorphic to some L(G)) are explicitly noted as unresolved in the literature on model theory of operator algebras.

status_evidence.title: A gentle introduction to von Neumann algebras for model theorists
status_evidence.snippet: Whether R^ω is isomorphic to L(G) for some group G is posed as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The related question of whether an ultrapower of the hyperfinite II_1 factor is a group von Neumann algebra is open.

status_evidence.title: Ultraproducts of von Neumann Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing structural properties of ultrapowers of II_1 factors with many open questions remaining.
status_evidence.claim: Structural classification of ultrapowers as group von Neumann algebras is unresolved.
